requirement_text.REQ-062: Port SPC-01's RUNTIME half from src/engine/instance.zig -- the half shipped REQ-032 explicitly deferred to this stage. REQ-032's own description and acceptance criteria state that SPC-01 "belongs to S3 (src/engine/ port) since it requires a running instance/token model that doesn't exist yet" and name src/engine/instance.zig as its future integration point; REQ-032 ported only the SPC-02 definition-time half (parse_interface, validate_schema_shape). This requirement closes that loop. Two requirements in this same batch already presuppose it: REQ-044 ports Token.waiting_child_instance_id, and REQ-059 AC6 requires child-instance pin inheritance -- neither has a child-creation path to hang off without this. Port (R-Co source paths verified directly against src/engine/instance.zig and src/engine/transition.zig): - Child instance creation: createWithParentInheritance() (~L562, whose own comment states it is "called only from startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx() -- never exposed on the public API surface"), driven by startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx() (~L4668). Port that same non-public shape: sub-process child creation is an internal engine path, not a second public start entry point alongside REQ-045's create/1. - The sub_process_start PendingEvent that REQ-044's transition kernel emits when a token enters a SUB_PROCESS node (transition.zig's processNodeEntry SUB_PROCESS branch, which returns early if the parent token is already waiting on a child), and its consumption here. - The parent-token wait: the token's waiting_child_instance_id is set while the child runs and cleared on the sub_process_completed event (transition.zig ~L897 handles that event; the token-copy note at ~L678 records a real bug, R-Co's GH #428, where waiting_child_instance_id was dropped during token copying -- port the field preservation carefully, since losing it silently strands the parent forever). - buildSubProcessChildInitialVars() (~L4544): SPC-01's input filtering. When the SUB_PROCESS node declares an interface, ONLY the named inputs are copied into the child's initial variable map, each validated against its json_schema first; when it declares none, EXT-05 behaviour applies unchanged (the full parent variable map is copied). Use REQ-032's already-shipped parse/validate functions for the interface itself rather than re-parsing it. - Completion propagation: on child COMPLETED, only the variables named in interface.outputs merge into the parent per REQ-049's EE-09 merge; every other variable the child produced is DISCARDED, not merged. With no declared interface, the full child map merges back (EXT-05). - The four SPC-01 failure modes, each a distinct error routing into REQ-061's EE-10 path (instance.zig's error enum at L258-272 and the code mapping at L4147-4155): SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_INPUT, SUB_PROCESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION (both at activation -- the parent goes to ERROR and NO child instance is created, so no orphan), SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_OUTPUT, SUB_PROCESS_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION (both at completion -- the parent goes to ERROR and the merge is not applied, not partially applied). RELATIONSHIP TO REQ-059: a child instance inherits its parent's pin set (PIN-04 AC2/AC3), which REQ-059 already specifies -- and createWithParentInheritance() is the function that carries it. This requirement owns child creation and the interface contract; REQ-059 owns what the pin entries contain and how conflicts are recorded. Neither should re-implement the other's half; state the seam in the moduledoc. SCOPE BOUNDARY: R-Co's EE-08 documents that cancelling a parent does NOT cancel its child -- port that documented behaviour rather than inventing a cascade. No HTTP surface is added: sub-processes are started by the engine, never by a route. There is no public sub-process start endpoint to defer to S4 in the first place -- say so in the moduledoc, so a later reader does not go looking for one.

task.description: Design the SPC-01 runtime half: child instance creation (internal-only, driven from the engine's own dispatch of a SUB_PROCESS node entry, not a public API), parent-token wait/clear of waiting_child_instance_id, input-filter-on-activation, output-merge-on-completion, and the four failure modes routed through REQ-061's set_instance_error path. Branch feature/WF02-REQ062-20260819 already exists and is checked out (Step 00 PASSED). Read lib/letflow/engine.ex, lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, lib/letflow/engine/token.ex, lib/letflow/engine/token_record.ex, lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/sub_process_interface.ex (REQ-032's already-shipped interface parse/validate), lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex (REQ-049's merge), and lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex + lib/letflow/process_instance.ex (to understand the existing one-process-per-instance supervision shape a new child instance must join) before designing. Also read docs/migration/stage-3-instance-engine.md and docs/migration/decisions/ for anything on record about sub-process/child-instance shape.
acceptance_criteria: a token entering a SUB_PROCESS node with a declared interface creates exactly one child instance whose initial variable map contains ONLY the declared inputs -- a parent variable not named in inputs is demonstrably absent from the child
a SUB_PROCESS node with no declared interface copies the full parent variable map to the child (EXT-05 behaviour preserved), demonstrated by an explicit test alongside the filtered case

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes has its own test and its own distinct error: the two activation failures leave ZERO child instances created (verified by counting instance rows), and the two completion failures leave the parent's variable map unmodified (no partial merge)

on child completion with a declared interface.outputs, only the named outputs merge into the parent via REQ-049's merge, and a child variable not named in outputs is demonstrably absent from the parent afterwards

the parent token's waiting_child_instance_id is set while the child runs and cleared on completion, and it survives a transition that copies tokens for an unrelated reason -- an explicit regression test for R-Co's GH #428 field-dropping bug
child instance creation is not reachable through REQ-045's public create/1 path, matching R-Co's internal-only createWithParentInheritance shape, confirmed by inspection and stated in the moduledoc
cancelling a parent instance does not cancel its running child, matching R-Co's documented EE-08 behaviour, demonstrated by an explicit test rather than assumed

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes is demonstrated routing into REQ-061's set_instance_error rather than writing its own ERROR transition, confirmed by inspection and by test -- this closes REQ-061's own AC obligation, deferred forward because REQ-062 did not exist when REQ-061 was built

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req062-sub-process-runtime.md covering the SPC-01 runtime half. AC mapping: (1) interface-filtered input copy -> design 3.2.1 build_child_initial_variables/2; (2) no-interface full-map EXT-05 copy -> 3.2.1's interface==nil clause; (3) four failure modes, zero child instances on activation failures, no partial merge on completion failures -> 3.2.1/3.2.2/3.2.3/4 (summary table) plus 3.3's 'append_start_multi/6 never called on {:error,_}' and 3.4 step 2's 'no Multi step appended before the merge-variable check'; (4) output-merge-only-named-outputs -> 3.2.2/3.4 step 3; (5) waiting_child_instance_id set/clear/preserve incl. GH-428 regression invariant -> section 5 plus 1.1's struct-update discipline; (6) internal-only child creation, no public create/2 second entry point -> 0's scope boundary plus 3.3's append_start_multi contract (Multi-composable, never opens its own transaction, never called from any public function); (7) EE-08 parent-cancel-does-not-cascade -> section 7 (confirms zero code change needed, since cancel_instance/3's existing instance_id-scoped filters already exclude child rows); (8) four failure modes routed through ExecutionError.append_multi, not a bespoke ERROR transition -> section 3.2.3 + section 4 table. REQ-059 pin-inheritance seam stated (parent_instance_id threaded to the child INSTANCE_STARTED call site) without implementing REQ-059's own pin-conflict logic, per section 8. Four open questions listed explicitly in section 9 (OQ-1: SUB_PROCESS node's definition-reference attribute is unverified/assumed, flagged not guessed-silently; OQ-2: whether registry variable-type schemas also apply to sub-process output merge; OQ-3: unbounded cross-definition recursion depth; OQ-4: child-cancelled-directly leaves parent waiting forever, no cascade specified). No implementation code included -- signatures/@spec/type shapes and DB migration snippets (schema DDL, not app logic) only.
